newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW - SABRE, Gulfstream due, demand still heated.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - SABRE, Gulfstream due, demand still heated.

text.p: This week's initial public offerings sector will be dominated by two huge offerings from corporate jetmaker Gulfstream Aerospace Corp and SABRE Group Holdings Inc.
The companies are planning mammoth IPOs worth over a billion dollars on a combined basis and SABRE's could sizzle.

"This is the best stock on the board this week," said David Menlow, president of the IPO Financial Network in Springfield, New Jersey. He said SABRE could immediately jump three to five points when it begins trading.
SABRE, the computer reservations and information subsidiary of AMR Corp, will be one of the 10 largest computer services firm in terms of market capitalization after the offering.

The deal values SABRE at about $2.56 billion to $2.94 billion according to Brian Harris, an airline analyst with Lehman Brothers, within range of his estimates. SABRE plans to offer 20.2 million shares in a range of $20 to $23 each

Gulfstream Aerospace will go public in a $644 million deal this week, but looming competition is expected to crimp its opening premiums. It could fetch up to a point in early trading, IPO analysts say.

Its new long-range G-V aircraft has enjoyed a one-year lead on the competition, but its potential market will shrink starting in 1997 as Boeing Co and Canada's Bombardier Inc launch comparable products, some aerospace analysts said. The G-V jets sell for a hefty price of over $30 million apiece.
Other offerings that could be hot next week are Trusted Information Systems Inc by J.P. Morgan & Co, Lason Holdings, and Superior Consultant Holdings Corp analysts said.
John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket, says Splash Technology Holdings Inc by Alex. Brown, Donnelley Enterprises Solutions Inc, Spatial Technology, and Kitty Hawk Inc could pick up premiums.

"I like Kitty Hawk very much," said Manish Shah of the IPO Aftermarket. "You always make more money transporting freight rather than people. And a similar deal, Atlas Air tripled since it went last public."

Shah also says Hibbett Sporting Goods Inc could be a strong pick for long-term investors. "What is unique about them is that they tie in promotions with local sports games, creating a lot of traffic. It's very clever."
Smith Barney is the lead underwriter of the offering, which is expected to price in a range of $14 to $16.
"It's a little expensive, but they have nice revenue and earnings growth," Shah said.
Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at Amas Securities, says she likes White Pine Software Inc, a company that makes connectivity software.

Farley says the IPO market, while picking up, is still cautious. "Investor confidence has returned, but it is still selective. We're starting to see some fairly high voume in these showing there are a lot of buyers, and allocations are getting smaller," she said.
Another huge IPO that could come as early as next week is Ingram Micro Inc, a computer reseller with $8 billion in yearly sales, according to Menlow.

"It's going to be an okay market until November, when it will get ugly," Menlow said. "It's such a large quantity of offerings ... Secondaries have really been doing a lot better in the IPO market, because allocations have gotten much smaller and secondaries have a stronger level of comfort," he said.
